L1@P0: 11 September 2023 CRN00D114 Page 1 of 18
L2@P0: Summary of Product Characteristics
L3@P0: 1 NAME OF THE MEDICINAL PRODUCT
L4@P0: Mitoxana 1 g Powder for Sterile Concentrate
L5@P0: 2 QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE COMPOSITION
L6@P0: Each vial contains 1 g of ifosfamide.
L7@P0: When reconstituted as directed, each millilitre of concentrate contains 80 mg Ifosfamide.
L8@P0: For full list of excipients, see section 6.1
L9@P0: 3 PHARMACEUTICAL FORM
L10@P0: Powder for concentrate for solution for infusion or injection. (Powder for Sterile Concentrate).
L11@P0: White powder.
L12@P0: 4 CLINICAL PARTICULARS
L13@P0: 4.1 Therapeutic indications
L14@P0: Mitoxana is a cytotoxic drug for the treatment of malignant disease. As a single agent it has successfully produced objective
L15@P0: remissions in a wide range of malignant conditions. Mitoxana is also frequently used in combination with other cytotoxic drugs,
L16@P0: radiotherapy and surgery.
L17@P0: Children and adolescents – see section 5.1 - Paediatric Population.
L18@P0: 4.2 Posology and method of administration
L19@P0: Ifosfamide should be administered only by physicians experienced with this drug.
L20@P0: Dosage must be individualised. Doses and duration of treatment and/or treatment intervals depend on the therapeutic
L21@P0: indication, the scheme of a combination therapy, the patient's general state of health and organ function, and the results of
L22@P0: laboratory monitoring.
L23@P0: Method of administration
L24@P0: A guide to the dosage regimens used for most indications is given below:
L25@P0: a)  8 - 12 g/m² equally fractionated as single daily doses over 3 - 5 days every 2 - 4 weeks.
L26@P0: b)  5 - 6 g/m² (maximum 10 g) given as a 24 hour infusion every 3 - 4 weeks.
L27@P0: The frequency of dosage is determined by the degree of myelosuppression and the time taken to recover adequate bone
L28@P0: marrow function. The usual number of courses given is 4, but up to 7 (6 by 24 hour infusion) courses have been
L29@P0: given. Re-treatment has been given following relapse.
L30@P0: In combination with other agents of similar toxicity, a dose reduction or extension of the therapy-free intervals may be
L31@P0: necessary.
L32@P0: During or immediately after administration, adequate amounts of fluid should be ingested or infused to force diuresis in order
L33@P0: to reduce the risk of urothelial toxicity (see section 4.4).
L34@P0-1: For prophylaxis of hemorrhagic cystitis, ifosfamide should be used in combination with mesna.Health Products Regulatory Authority
L35@P1: 11 September 2023 CRN00D114 Page 2 of 18
L36@P1: Parenteral drug products should be inspected visually for particulate matter and discoloration prior to administration.
L37@P1: Before parenteral administration, the substance must be completely dissolved. For instructions on dilution of the medicinal
L38@P1: product before administration, see section 6.6.
L39@P1: For storage conditions of Mitoxana reconstituted in Water for Injection and further diluted in 0.9% Sodium Chloride, refer to
L40@P1: section 6.3.
L41@P1: Patients with Renal Impairment:
L42@P1: The dose may need to be adjusted in patients with decreased renal function (see sections 4.3 and 4.4).
L43@P1: Ifosfamide and its metabolites are dialyzable. In patients requiring dialysis, use of a consistent interval between ifosfamide
L44@P1: administration and dialysis should be considered.
L45@P1: Patients with Hepatic Impairment:
L46@P1: The dose may need to be adjusted in patients with decreased hepatic function (see sections 4.3 and 4.4).
L47@P1: Elderly:
L48@P1: In general, dose selection for an elderly patient should be cautious, reflecting the greater frequency of decreased hepatic, renal
L49@P1: or cardiac function, and of concomitant disease or other drug therapy (see section 5.2).
L50@P1: Paediatric:
L51@P1: In children, the dosage and administration should be determined by the tumour type, tumour stage, the general condition of
L52@P1: the patient, any previous cytotoxic therapy, and whether chemotherapy or radiotherapy is to be administered
L53@P1: concurrently. Clinical trials have involved doses of:
L54@P1: a)  5 g/m² over 24 hours
L55@P1: b)  9 g/m² equally fractionated as single daily doses over 5 days
L56@P1: c)  9 g/m² as a continuous infusion over 72 hours - repeated at three weekly intervals.
L57@P1: 4.3 Contraindications
L58@P1: Ifosfamide is contra-indicated in patients with:
L59@P1: • Known hypersensitivity to ifosfamide. See section 4.4
L60@P1: • Urinary outflow obstruction.
L61@P1: Mitoxana should only be administered when there are facilities for regular monitoring of clinical, biochemical and
L62@P1: haematological parameters before, during and after administration and under the direction of a specialist oncology service.
L63@P1: Mitoxana is contra-indicated in patients with known hypersensitivity to ifosfamide, bone marrow aplasia, myelosuppression,
L64@P1: urinary tract obstruction, acute infections including urinary tract infection, or with acute urothelial toxicity from cytotoxic
L65@P1: chemotherapy or radiation therapy.
L66@P1: Mitoxana is contra-indicated in patients with renal impairment (serum creatinine greater than 120 mcmol/l or 1.5 mg/100 ml)
L67@P1: or hepatic impairment (bilirubin greater than 17 mcmol/l or 1 mg/100 ml), or serum transaminases or alkaline phosphatase
L68@P1: more than 2.5 times the upper limit of normal.
L69@P1: 4.4 Special warnings and precautions for use
L70@P1: In individual patients, risk factors for ifosfamide toxicities and their sequelae described here and in other sections may
L71@P1: constitute contraindications. In such situations, individual assessment of risk and expected benefits is necessary. Adverse
L72@P1-2: reactions, depending on their severity, may require dosage modification or discontinuation of treatmentHealth Products Regulatory Authority
L73@P2: 11 September 2023 CRN00D114 Page 3 of 18
L74@P2: WARNINGS
L75@P2: Myelosuppression, Immunosuppression, Infections
L76@P2: Treatment with ifosfamide may cause myelosuppression and significant suppression of immune responses, which can lead to
L77@P2: severe infections. Fatal outcome of ifosfamide-associated myelosuppression has been reported.
L78@P2: Ifosfamide-induced myelosuppression can cause leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia (associated with a higher risk of
L79@P2: bleeding events), and anaemia
L80@P2: Administration of ifosfamide is normally followed by a reduction in the leukocyte count. The nadir of the leukocyte count tends
L81@P2: to be reached approximately during the second week after administration. Subsequently, the leukocyte count rises again.
L82@P2: Severe myelosuppression and immunosuppression must be expected particularly in patients pre-treated with and/or receiving
L83@P2: concomitant chemotherapy/haematotoxic agents, immunosuppressants and/or radiation therapy (see section 4.5).
L84@P2: Where indicated, use of haematopoiesis-stimulating agents (colony-stimulating factors and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents)
L85@P2: may be considered to reduce the risk of myelosuppressive complications and/or help facilitate the delivery of the intended
L86@P2: dosing. For information on a potential interaction with G-CSF and GM-CSF (granulocyte colony-stimulating factor, granulocyte
L87@P2: macrophage colony-stimulating factor) (see section 4.5)
L88@P2: The risk of myelosuppression is dose dependent and is increased with administration of a single high dose compared to
L89@P2: fractionated administration.
L90@P2: The risk of myelosuppression is increased in patients with reduced renal function.
L91@P2: Severe immunosuppression has led to serious, sometimes fatal, infections.  Infections reported with ifosfamide include
L92@P2: pneumonias, as well as other bacterial, fungal, viral, and parasitic infections. Sepsis and septic shock also have been reported.
L93@P2: Latent infections can be reactivated. In patients treated with ifosfamide, reactivation has been reported for various viral
L94@P2: infections.
L95@P2: Antimicrobial prophylaxis may be indicated in certain cases of neutropenia at the discretion of the managing physician.
L96@P2: Close hematologic monitoring is recommended. White blood cell count, platelet count, and haemoglobin levels should be
L97@P2: obtained prior to each administration and at appropriate intervals after administration.
L98@P2: Encephalopathy and CNS toxicityAdministration of ifosfamide can cause  encephalopathy and other neurotoxic effects
L99@P2: An ifosfamide-induced CNS toxicity may become manifest within a few hours to a few days after administration and in most
L100@P2: cases resolves within 48 to 72 hours of ifosfamide discontinuation. Symptoms may persist for longer periods of time.
L101@P2: Occasionally, recovery has been incomplete. Fatal outcome of CNS toxicity has been reported. If CNS toxicity develops,
L102@P2: administration of ifosfamide should be discontinued.
L103@P2: CNS toxicity seems to be dose dependent. Risk factors for the development of ifosfamide associated encephalopathy include
L104@P2: hypoalbuminaemia, impaired renal function, poor performance status, pelvic disease (e.g. presence of tumour in lower
L105@P2: abdomen, bulky abdominal disease), and previous or concomitant nephrotoxic treatments including cisplatin.
L106@P2: Due to the potential for additive effects, drugs acting on the CNS (such as antiemetics, sedatives, narcotics, or antihistamines)
L107@P2: or substances (such as alcohol) acting on the CNS must be used with particular caution or, if necessary, be discontinued in case
L108@P2: of ifosfamide induced encephalopathy.Patients treated with ifosfamide should be closely monitored for symptoms of
L109@P2: encephalopathies in particular if patients are at increased risk for encephalopathies.
L110@P2: The use of methylene blue may be considered for the treatment and prophylaxis of ifosfamide-associated encephalopathies.
L111@P2: Renal and Urothelial Toxicity
L112@P2: Ifosfamide is both nephrotoxic and urotoxic.
L113@P2: Glomerular and tubular kidney function must be evaluated and checked before commencement of therapy, as well as during
L114@P2-3: and after treatment.Health Products Regulatory Authority
L115@P3: 11 September 2023 CRN00D114 Page 4 of 18
L116@P3: Urinary sediment should be checked regularly for the presence of erythrocytes and other signs of uro/nephrotoxicity.
L117@P3: Close clinical monitoring of serum and urine chemistries, including phosphorus, potassium, and other laboratory parameters
L118@P3: appropriate for identifying nephrotoxicity and urothelial toxicity is recommended.
L119@P3: Nephrotoxic Effects
L120@P3: Fatal outcome from nephrotoxicity has been documented.
L121@P3: Renal parenchymal and tubular necrosis have been reported in patients treated with ifosfamide.
L122@P3: Disorders of renal function (glomerular and tubular) following ifosfamide administration are very common (see section 4.8).
L123@P3: Manifestations include a decrease in glomerular filtration rate and an increase in serum creatinine, proteinuria, enzymuria,
L124@P3: cylindruria, aminoaciduria, phosphaturia, and glycosuria as well as renal tubular acidosis. Fanconi syndrome, renal rickets, and
L125@P3: growth retardation in children as well as osteomalacia in adults have also been reported.
L126@P3: Development of a syndrome resembling SIADH (syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion) has been reported
L127@P3: with ifosfamide.
L128@P3: Tubular damage may become apparent during therapy, months or even years after cessation of treatment.
L129@P3: Glomerular or tubular dysfunction may resolve with time, remain stable, or progress over a period of months or years, even
L130@P3: after completion of ifosfamide treatment. Acute tubular necrosis, acute renal failure, and chronic renal failure secondary to
L131@P3: ifosfamide therapy have been reported (see section 4.8).
L132@P3: The risk of developing clinical manifestations of nephrotoxicity is increased with, for example:
L133@P3:  large cumulative doses of ifosfamide,
L134@P3:  pre-existing renal impairment,
L135@P3:  prior or concurrent treatment with potentially nephrotoxic agents,
L136@P3:  younger age in children (particularly in children up to approximately 5 years of age),
L137@P3:  reduced nephron reserve as in patients with renal tumours and those having  undergone renal radiation or
L138@P3: unilateral nephrectomy.
L139@P3: The risks and expected benefits of ifosfamide therapy should be carefully weighed when considering the use of ifosfamide in
L140@P3: patients with pre-existing renal impairment or reduced nephron reserve (see section 4.3).
L141@P3: Urothelial Effects
L142@P3: Ifosfamide administration is associated with urotoxic effects, which can be reduced by prophylactic use of mesna.
L143@P3: Hemorrhagic cystitis requiring blood transfusion has been reported with ifosfamide.
L144@P3: The risk of hemorrhagic cystitis is dose-dependent and increased with administration of single high doses compared to
L145@P3: fractionated administration.
L146@P3: Hemorrhagic cystitis after a single dose of ifosfamide has been reported.
L147@P3: Before starting treatment, it is necessary to exclude or correct any urinary tract obstructions (see section 4.3).
L148@P3: During or immediately after administration, adequate amounts of fluid should be ingested or infused to force diuresis in order
L149@P3: to reduce the risk of urinary tract toxicity.
L150@P3: For prophylaxis of hemorrhagic cystitis, ifosfamide should be used in combination with mesna.
L151@P3-4: Ifosfamide should be used with caution, if at all, in patients with active urinary tract infections.Health Products Regulatory Authority
L152@P4: 11 September 2023 CRN00D114 Page 5 of 18
L153@P4: Past or concomitant radiation of the bladder or busulfan treatment may increase the risk for hemorrhagic cystitis.
L154@P4: The following manifestations of urotoxicity from cyclophosphamide, another oxazaphosphorine cytotoxic agent have been
L155@P4: reported:
L156@P4:  hemorrhagic cystitis (including severe forms with ulceration and necrosis),
L157@P4:  fatal outcome of urothelial toxicity, as well as the need for cystectomy due to fibrosis, bleeding, or secondary
L158@P4: malignancy.
L159@P4:  hematuria, which may be severe and recurrent; while hematuria usually resolves in a few days after treatment is
L160@P4: stopped, it may persist.
L161@P4:  signs of urothelial irritation (such as painful micturition, a feeling of residual urine, frequent voiding, nocturia,
L162@P4: urinary incontinence) as well as the development of bladder fibrosis, small-capacity bladder, telangiectasia, and
L163@P4: signs of chronic bladder irritation.
L164@P4:  pyelitis and ureteritis
